concerns.text: T011a-1a outputs an 'Intermediate list of triples' (in-memory) but T011a-1b requires consuming 'extracted triples' to write `data/intermediate/graphs_raw.json`. There is no task defined to persist the output of T011a-1a to a file before T011a-1b attempts to read it, creating a broken data-flow dependency.

T011c (Generate Noisy Graph) depends on T011b (Implement Noise Injection Logic). However, T011b is marked as [US1] and T011c is also [US1], but T011b is listed *after* T011a-2 (Schema Validation) which depends on T011a-1b. The logical flow requires T011b to be available *before* T011c runs. While T011b is listed before T011c, the dependency chain T011a-1b -> T011a-2 -> T011b -> T011c is valid, BUT T011b is marked [P] (parallel-safe) while it produces the core function `inject_noise` consumed by T011c. If T011c runs in parallel with T011b (as [P] implies), it will fail. T011b must be a strict prerequisite, not parallel-safe with its consumer.

T039 (Verify Seeds) depends on T011a-1b, T011c. However, T039 is marked [P] (parallel-safe). T039 reads the output of T011c (`graph_noise_42.json`). If T039 runs in parallel with T011c, it will read a non-existent or partial file. T039 cannot be parallel-safe relative to T011c.

T019b (Greedy Runner) depends on T019a (Lazy Runner) in the dependency list? No, it lists T011a, T011a-1b, T012, T018, T006. However, T019c (Noisy Lazy) and T019d (Noisy Greedy) depend on T011c (Noisy Graph). T011c is in US1. T019c/d are in US2. This is a valid cross-story dependency. However, T019b (Greedy Runner) is listed as dependent on T019a (Lazy Runner) in the 'Dependencies & Execution Order' section? No, the section says 'User stories can then proceed in parallel'. But T019b is listed as dependent on T019a in the task list? No, T019b depends on T018. The issue is T019c and T019d depend on T011c. T011c is in US1. If US1 is not complete, US2 cannot run noisy tests. This is a valid dependency, but the [P] tag on T019c/d might be misleading if T011c is not yet complete. The real issue is T019b (Greedy Runner) is marked [P] but depends on T018 (Greedy Strategy). T018 is [P]. This is fine. The main issue is T011b marked [P] while being a producer for T011c.

T017 (Lazy Traversal) is marked [P]. However, it depends on T012 (Full Strategy) and T004 (Graph Utils). If T012 is not complete, T017 cannot run. The [P] tag implies it can run in parallel with other tasks, but it has a strict dependency on T012. This is a minor semantic issue with the [P] tag usage, as [P] usually means 'no dependencies on other tasks in the same phase', but here it depends on a task in the same phase (T012). T012 is in US1, T017 is in US2. If US1 and US2 are parallel, T017 cannot start until T012 is done. The [P] tag is technically incorrect if it implies independence from T012.
